articles.title: EU regulators fine Apple over App Store steering rules
articles.text: The European Commission fined Apple 1.8 billion euros, saying its App Store rules stopped music streaming apps from telling users about cheaper subscriptions elsewhere. Apple said it would appeal. Analysts said the decision adds regulatory risk to the services segment, which has been the company's main source of margin growth, and could encourage similar cases under the Digital Markets Act. Several developers welcomed the ruling and said they expect to change their in-app pricing messages in Europe within months.

articles.title: Apple's iPhone revenue tops estimates on India demand
articles.text: Apple reported fourth-quarter iPhone revenue above analyst estimates, helped by record sales in India and a strong start for its newest models. Gross margin came in at the high end of guidance. Chief Financial Officer comments pointed to continued supply constraints on the premium model through December. Shares rose four percent in after-hours trading.

articles.title: Apple supplier warns of chip shortage affecting Mac production
articles.text: A major Apple supplier warned that a shortage of advanced packaging capacity could delay Mac laptop shipments into the first quarter. The supplier said it was adding capacity but that lead times had stretched to twenty weeks. Analysts estimated the delay could shift several hundred thousand Mac units out of the holiday quarter.

articles.title: Apple expands buyback and raises dividend
articles.text: Apple's board authorised an additional 100 billion dollars of share repurchases and raised the quarterly dividend by four percent. The company said it remains committed to a net cash neutral position over time.

articles.title: Tesla recalls 200,000 vehicles over power steering fault
articles.text: Tesla is recalling about 200,000 vehicles in the United States because a software fault can cause a loss of power steering assist at low speeds, according to a filing with the national highway safety regulator. The company said an over-the-air software update will fix the issue and that it is not aware of any crashes linked to the fault.

articles.title: Tesla deliveries fall short as price cuts squeeze margins
articles.text: Tesla delivered fewer vehicles than analysts expected in the third quarter, despite price cuts in China and Europe. Analysts warned that automotive gross margins could fall below fifteen percent if discounting continues, and that competition from lower-cost Chinese electric vehicle makers is intensifying.

articles.title: Tesla energy storage deployments hit a record
articles.text: Tesla's energy storage business deployed a record amount of battery capacity in the quarter, driven by utility-scale Megapack projects in Texas and Australia. The storage unit now carries higher margins than the car business.

articles.title: Microsoft Azure growth accelerates on AI workloads
articles.text: Microsoft said revenue from its Azure cloud platform grew thirty-five percent, faster than the previous quarter, as customers expanded AI workloads. The company said data centre capacity remains tight and that capital expenditure will rise again next quarter.

articles.title: Microsoft faces FTC probe into cloud licensing
articles.text: The US Federal Trade Commission opened an investigation into whether Microsoft's software licensing terms make it harder for customers to move workloads to rival cloud providers. Microsoft said it would cooperate. Legal experts said the probe could take more than a year and might lead to changes in how Windows Server and Office licences are priced on other clouds.

articles.title: Microsoft to cut 2,000 jobs in gaming division
articles.text: Microsoft plans to cut about 2,000 jobs in its gaming division as it consolidates studios after recent acquisitions. The company said it would focus on fewer, larger game franchises and its subscription service.

articles.title: Amazon Web Services outage disrupts major websites
articles.text: A multi-hour outage in an Amazon Web Services region disrupted streaming, banking and retail websites. Amazon blamed a networking configuration change and said it would publish a full incident review. Some enterprise customers said they would revisit plans to spread workloads across multiple regions.

articles.title: Amazon raises holiday hiring and expects record Prime sales
articles.text: Amazon said it would hire 250,000 seasonal workers for the holiday period and expects record sales during its Prime shopping event. The company is expanding same-day delivery to more cities.

articles.title: Union drive gains ground at Amazon warehouses
articles.text: Workers at three Amazon warehouses filed for union elections, citing injury rates and scheduling. Labour analysts said a successful vote could raise fulfilment costs and lead to more organising across the company's logistics network.
